strings.name: Elizabeth Blackburn
strings.summary: Elizabeth Blackburn's work on Tetrahymena identified repeated DNA sequences at chromosome ends and, with Jack Szostak, Carol Greider and others, explored how those ends are protected and maintained. She co-discovered telomerase with Greider, illuminating links among cell replication, ageing and disease. The three shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Understanding telomere mechanisms does not itself establish a life-extension treatment.

strings.influence.rationale: Advanced research on telomeres and telomerase, deepening scientific understanding of cellular aging, chromosome stability and disease mechanisms.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: University of Melbourne biochemistry bachelor's (1970), master's (1972); Cambridge PhD (1975)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Protection of chromosome ends
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: With Szostak and others, showed how specialized telomeric DNA protects chromosome ends.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Co-discovery of telomerase
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Identified the telomere-extending enzyme with Greider, connecting DNA replication and chromosome stability.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Research reflections in Kyoto
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Joined John Sedat for lectures on telomeres, scientific collaboration and their experiences in research careers.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Became Salk president
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Began leading the Salk Institute and later became president emerita.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Shared Nobel medicine prize
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Honored with Greider and Szostak for discoveries concerning telomeres and telomerase.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Moved to UCSF
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Moved from Berkeley to UC San Francisco to continue telomere and chromosome research.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Detected telomerase activity
strings.timeline.event-5.text: With Greider, detected telomere-extending activity in Tetrahymena extracts, then validated and published the result.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Demonstrated telomere protection
strings.timeline.event-6.text: With Szostak, used yeast experiments to show that Tetrahymena telomere sequences protect linear chromosomes.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Telomere sequence and Berkeley
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Work with Joseph Gall identified repeated telomeric sequences; she joined Berkeley's faculty that year.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Cambridge doctorate
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Completed doctoral work in Frederick Sanger's research environment before postdoctoral work at Yale.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Melbourne bachelor's degree
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Completed undergraduate biochemistry, followed by a1972master's and doctoral study in Britain.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Hobart
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Hobart, Tasmania, into a family connected with medicine and science.
